name: 2019 livery
description: White fuselage with very large thin lower-case 'virgin atlantic' in deep slate purple running from behind the cockpit to the wing, repeated under the belly. All-red fin with the white Virgin signature, the red flowing down over the fuselage under the fin. Red engines, red wingtips. The flying lady holding a Union flag under the cockpit.

areas.name: red under the fin, wrapping down the aft fuselage

logos.description: The flying lady nose art (2019): a woman leaping forward, one arm raised, the other holding a big Union flag that waves aft of her, behind the cockpit windows at about the windows' height; the aircraft's name in small script under her.

titles.style: Very large thin monoline lower-case letters, upright and loosely spaced: round, open forms (a single-storey a, its bowl hung from a flat bar; a g with an open tail), the stems' tops cut on a slant; the baseline at the bottom of the windows and the ascenders near the crown. Not the script of the fin.
The same thin lower-case title under the forward belly, read from below.

The Virgin signature: a hand-lettered script, a tall V with a ball at its top, the letters leaning and rising about 25° along the fin, a long swash under them crossed by the g's descender. It reads normally on both sides and rises toward the tail on the left side and toward the nose on the right.
The same signature on the right side: rising toward the nose, so it's turned the other way and starts aft.

notes: The Virgin signature on the fin is a script wordmark, drawn as a title (two: it rises toward the tail on the left side and toward the nose on the right, G-VAHH) that names its mark. Re-measured 2026-11-22: the fuselage lettering is about 8.4 times as long as its l is tall (G-VOWS, by its window row); on G-VTEA it runs x 0.12-0.47 with the l's top at the crown, so its height is 0.92 (it was 0.62, which spread the letters half as wide again); the belly's the same size. The fuselage and belly lettering isn't the script: thin upright lower-case letters for both words (G-VOWS, G-VCRU). Earlier 'silver' scheme (silver-gray fuselage, red 'virgin atlantic' titles, red tail) is still on part of the 787-9 and remaining A330-300 fleet; not drawn here. The red wrap's lower edge is seen from below only at a distance. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on G-VTEA: the title's lowercase about 0.7 of the l's height; the red wrap's lower edge drawn as a curve. The fuselage title is thin outlined lettering: the reference renderer, spreading a stand-in to the measured length, draws it heavier than it is.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (purple belly, red bands). The 2019 livery (white body, purple titles) replaced the silver scheme flown since 2006, from G-VLUX onward.
